content.text: Enter Adriana, wife to Antipholus (of Ephesus) with Luciana her sister.

lines.text: Neither my husband nor the slave return'd
lines.plainText: Neither my husband nor the slave return'd

lines.text: That in such haste I sent to seek his master?
lines.plainText: That in such haste I sent to seek his master

lines.text: Sure, Luciana, it is two o'clock.
lines.plainText: Sure Luciana it is two o'clock

lines.text: Perhaps some merchant hath invited him,
lines.plainText: Perhaps some merchant hath invited him

lines.text: And from the mart he's somewhere gone to dinner.
lines.plainText: And from the mart he's somewhere gone to dinner

lines.text: Good sister, let us dine, and never fret;
lines.plainText: Good sister let us dine and never fret

lines.text: A man is master of his liberty;
lines.plainText: A man is master of his liberty

lines.text: Time is their master, and when they see time,
lines.plainText: Time is their master and when they see time

lines.text: They'll go or come. If so, be patient, sister.
lines.plainText: They'll go or come If so be patient sister

lines.text: Why should their liberty than ours be more?
lines.plainText: Why should their liberty than ours be more

lines.text: Because their business still lies out o' door.
lines.plainText: Because their business still lies out o' door

lines.text: Look when I serve him so, he takes it ill.
lines.plainText: Look when I serve him so he takes it ill

lines.text: O, know he is the bridle of your will.
lines.plainText: O know he is the bridle of your will

lines.text: There's none but asses will be bridled so.
lines.plainText: There's none but asses will be bridled so

lines.text: Why, headstrong liberty is lash'd with woe.
lines.plainText: Why headstrong liberty is lash'd with woe

lines.text: There's nothing situate under heaven's eye
lines.plainText: There's nothing situate under heaven's eye

lines.text: But hath his bound in earth, in sea, in sky.
lines.plainText: But hath his bound in earth in sea in sky

lines.text: The beasts, the fishes, and the winged fowls
lines.plainText: The beasts the fishes and the winged fowls

lines.text: Are their males' subjects, and at their controls.
lines.plainText: Are their males' subjects and at their controls

lines.text: Man, more divine, the masters of all these,
lines.plainText: Man more divine the masters of all these

lines.text: Lord of the wide world and wild wat'ry seas,
lines.plainText: Lord of the wide world and wild wat'ry seas

lines.text: Indued with intellectual sense and souls,
lines.plainText: Indued with intellectual sense and souls

lines.text: Of more pre-eminence than fish and fowls,
lines.plainText: Of more preeminence than fish and fowls

lines.text: Are masters to their females, and their lords:
lines.plainText: Are masters to their females and their lords

lines.text: Then let your will attend on their accords.
lines.plainText: Then let your will attend on their accords

lines.text: This servitude makes you to keep unwed.
lines.plainText: This servitude makes you to keep unwed

lines.text: Not this, but troubles of the marriage-bed.
lines.plainText: Not this but troubles of the marriagebed

lines.text: But, were you wedded, you would bear some sway.
lines.plainText: But were you wedded you would bear some sway

lines.text: Ere I learn love, I'll practise to obey.
lines.plainText: Ere I learn love I'll practise to obey

lines.text: How if your husband start some other where?
lines.plainText: How if your husband start some other where

lines.text: Till he come home again, I would forbear.
lines.plainText: Till he come home again I would forbear

lines.text: Patience unmov'd! No marvel though she pause;
lines.plainText: Patience unmov'd No marvel though she pause

lines.text: They can be meek that have no other cause.
lines.plainText: They can be meek that have no other cause

lines.text: A wretched soul bruis'd with adversity,
lines.plainText: A wretched soul bruis'd with adversity

lines.text: We bid be quiet when we hear it cry;
lines.plainText: We bid be quiet when we hear it cry

lines.text: But were we burd'ned with like weight of pain,
lines.plainText: But were we burd'ned with like weight of pain

lines.text: As much, or more, we should ourselves complain:
lines.plainText: As much or more we should ourselves complain

lines.text: So thou, that hast no unkind mate to grieve thee,
lines.plainText: So thou that hast no unkind mate to grieve thee

lines.text: With urging helpless patience would relieve me:
lines.plainText: With urging helpless patience would relieve me

lines.text: But if thou live to see like right bereft,
lines.plainText: But if thou live to see like right bereft

lines.text: This fool-begg'd patience in thee will be left.
lines.plainText: This foolbegg'd patience in thee will be left

lines.text: Well, I will marry one day, but to try.
lines.plainText: Well I will marry one day but to try

lines.text: Here comes your man, now is your husband nigh.
lines.plainText: Here comes your man now is your husband nigh

lines.text: Say, is your tardy master now at hand?
lines.plainText: Say is your tardy master now at hand

lines.text: Nay, he's at two hands with me, and that my two ears can witness.
lines.plainText: Nay he's at two hands with me and that my two ears can witness

lines.text: Say, didst thou speak with him? know'st thou his mind?
lines.plainText: Say didst thou speak with him know'st thou his mind

lines.text: Ay, ay, he told his mind upon mine ear.
lines.plainText: Ay ay he told his mind upon mine ear

lines.text: Beshrew his hand, I scarce could understand it.
lines.plainText: Beshrew his hand I scarce could understand it

lines.text: Spake he so doubtfully thou couldst not feel his meaning?
lines.plainText: Spake he so doubtfully thou couldst not feel his meaning

lines.text: Nay, he struck so plainly I could too well feel his blows; and withal so doubtfully that I could scarce understand them.
lines.plainText: Nay he struck so plainly I could too well feel his blows and withal so doubtfully that I could scarce understand them

lines.text: But say, I prithee, is he coming home?
lines.plainText: But say I prithee is he coming home

lines.text: It seems he hath great care to please his wife.
lines.plainText: It seems he hath great care to please his wife

lines.text: Why, mistress, sure my master is horn-mad.
lines.plainText: Why mistress sure my master is hornmad

lines.text: Horn-mad, thou villain?
lines.plainText: Hornmad thou villain

lines.text: I mean not cuckold-mad,
lines.plainText: I mean not cuckoldmad

lines.text: But sure he's stark mad.
lines.plainText: But sure he's stark mad

lines.text: When I desir'd him to come home to dinner,
lines.plainText: When I desir'd him to come home to dinner

lines.text: He ask'd me for a thousand marks in gold.
lines.plainText: He ask'd me for a thousand marks in gold

lines.text: "'Tis dinner time," quoth I. "My gold," quoth he.
lines.plainText: 'Tis dinner time quoth I My gold quoth he

lines.text: "Your meat doth burn" quoth I. "My gold," quoth he.
lines.plainText: Your meat doth burn quoth I My gold quoth he

lines.text: "Will you come home?" quoth I. "My gold," quoth he.
lines.plainText: Will you come home quoth I My gold quoth he

lines.text: "Where is the thousand marks I gave thee, villain?"
lines.plainText: Where is the thousand marks I gave thee villain

lines.text: "The pig" quoth I "is burn'd". "My gold," quoth he.
lines.plainText: The pig quoth I is burn'd My gold quoth he

lines.text: "My mistress, sir," quoth I. "Hang up thy mistress;
lines.plainText: My mistress sir quoth I Hang up thy mistress

lines.text: I know not thy mistress; out on thy mistress!"
lines.plainText: I know not thy mistress out on thy mistress

lines.text: Quoth who?
lines.plainText: Quoth who

lines.text: Quoth my master.
lines.plainText: Quoth my master

lines.text: "I know," quoth he, "no house, no wife, no mistress."
lines.plainText: I know quoth he no house no wife no mistress

lines.text: So that my errand, due unto my tongue,
lines.plainText: So that my errand due unto my tongue

lines.text: I thank him, I bare home upon my shoulders;
lines.plainText: I thank him I bare home upon my shoulders

lines.text: For, in conclusion, he did beat me there.
lines.plainText: For in conclusion he did beat me there

lines.text: Go back again, thou slave, and fetch him home.
lines.plainText: Go back again thou slave and fetch him home

lines.text: Go back again, and be new beaten home?
lines.plainText: Go back again and be new beaten home

lines.text: For God's sake, send some other messenger.
lines.plainText: For God's sake send some other messenger

lines.text: Back slave, or I will break thy pate across.
lines.plainText: Back slave or I will break thy pate across

lines.text: And he will bless that cross with other beating.
lines.plainText: And he will bless that cross with other beating

lines.text: Between you I shall have a holy head.
lines.plainText: Between you I shall have a holy head

lines.text: Hence, prating peasant. Fetch thy master home.
lines.plainText: Hence prating peasant Fetch thy master home

lines.text: Am I so round with you, as you with me,
lines.plainText: Am I so round with you as you with me

lines.text: That like a football you do spurn me thus?
lines.plainText: That like a football you do spurn me thus

lines.text: You spurn me hence, and he will spurn me hither.
lines.plainText: You spurn me hence and he will spurn me hither

lines.text: If I last in this service, you must case me in leather.
lines.plainText: If I last in this service you must case me in leather

lines.text: Fie, how impatience loureth in your face.
lines.plainText: Fie how impatience loureth in your face

lines.text: His company must do his minions grace,
lines.plainText: His company must do his minions grace

lines.text: Whilst I at home starve for a merry look.
lines.plainText: Whilst I at home starve for a merry look

lines.text: Hath homely age th' alluring beauty took
lines.plainText: Hath homely age th' alluring beauty took

lines.text: From my poor cheek? then he hath wasted it.
lines.plainText: From my poor cheek then he hath wasted it

lines.text: Are my discourses dull? barren my wit?
lines.plainText: Are my discourses dull barren my wit

lines.text: If voluble and sharp discourse be marr'd,
lines.plainText: If voluble and sharp discourse be marr'd

lines.text: Unkindness blunts it more than marble hard.
lines.plainText: Unkindness blunts it more than marble hard

lines.text: Do their gay vestments his affections bait?
lines.plainText: Do their gay vestments his affections bait

lines.text: That's not my fault; he's master of my state.
lines.plainText: That's not my fault he's master of my state

lines.text: What ruins are in me that can be found
lines.plainText: What ruins are in me that can be found

lines.text: By him not ruin'd? Then is he the ground
lines.plainText: By him not ruin'd Then is he the ground

lines.text: Of my defeatures. My decayed fair
lines.plainText: Of my defeatures My decayed fair

lines.text: A sunny look of his would soon repair;
lines.plainText: A sunny look of his would soon repair

lines.text: But, too unruly deer, he breaks the pale
lines.plainText: But too unruly deer he breaks the pale

lines.text: And feeds from home; poor I am but his stale.
lines.plainText: And feeds from home poor I am but his stale

lines.text: Self-harming jealousy! fie, beat it hence.
lines.plainText: Selfharming jealousy fie beat it hence

lines.text: Unfeeling fools can with such wrongs dispense.
lines.plainText: Unfeeling fools can with such wrongs dispense

lines.text: I know his eye doth homage otherwhere,
lines.plainText: I know his eye doth homage otherwhere

lines.text: Or else what lets it but he would be here?
lines.plainText: Or else what lets it but he would be here

lines.text: Sister, you know he promis'd me a chain;
lines.plainText: Sister you know he promis'd me a chain

lines.text: Would that alone, a love he would detain,
lines.plainText: Would that alone a love he would detain

lines.text: So he would keep fair quarter with his bed.
lines.plainText: So he would keep fair quarter with his bed

lines.text: I see the jewel best enamelled
lines.plainText: I see the jewel best enamelled

lines.text: Will lose his beauty; yet the gold bides still
lines.plainText: Will lose his beauty yet the gold bides still

lines.text: That others touch, yet often touching will
lines.plainText: That others touch yet often touching will

lines.text: Wear gold; and no man that hath a name
lines.plainText: Wear gold and no man that hath a name

lines.text: By falsehood and corruption doth it shame.
lines.plainText: By falsehood and corruption doth it shame

lines.text: Since that my beauty cannot please his eye,
lines.plainText: Since that my beauty cannot please his eye

lines.text: I'll weep what's left away, and weeping die.
lines.plainText: I'll weep what's left away and weeping die

lines.text: How many fond fools serve mad jealousy!
lines.plainText: How many fond fools serve mad jealousy
